subject: Production throttling: throttle-profile entanglement causing latency and 429s
messages:
From: Aventra Labs SRE <sre+ops@aventra.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.io, connor_obrien@redwood.io
Cc: erica.sanchez@aventra.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden spike in latency and 429s — urgent

Hi Jonas / Connor,

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and a growing number of 429 responses across our primary tenant traffic between 08:45 and 09:00 PDT this morning. Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to ~6% and p95 token latency jumped from 280ms to ~1.8s. We've attached a small sample of the request traces and 429 responses (prod-429-sample.csv).

This started right after a scheduled config change on our side (no changes to tokenization or model). Can you confirm if any routing or quota change on Redwood could cause cross-tenant contention or sudden request shaping? We're blocked for a critical customer demo at 10:30.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether any quota/burst policy changes were rolled in the last 24 hours?
- Any known issues with dedicated pool handoff / burst credit attribution?

Thanks,
Samir Patel
SRE, Aventra Labs
sre+ops@aventra.ai

Aventra Labs | Platform Reliability

Subject: Re: Production: sudden spike in latency and 429s — urgent

Samir — thanks for the flag and the CSV. I'm escalating immediately and looping in Neha (runtime/serving) and Marissa for visibility.

Quick notes:
- No scheduled infra deploy on our hosted fleet in that window that would cause a global policy shift.
- We've observed similar symptoms when quota attribution and burst windows for dedicated vs hosted pools become misaligned (requests get shunted into a tighter shaping regime).

Neha — can you review the attached sample and our current tenant policy snapshot? I'm attaching a config diff we pulled (policy-config-diff.txt) showing today's policy refresh. If we confirm a policy entanglement, we should plan a rollback and a one-hour mitigation (bump burst window + temporary per-tenant override).

Samir — we'll get you a short remediation ETA within 30 minutes.

Jonas Weber
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.io

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.io
To: jonas_weber@redwood.io, connor_obrien@redwood.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.io; Samir Patel <sre+ops@aventra.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Aug 2028 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden spike in latency and 429s — urgent

Investigated the traces and policy snapshot. TL;DR: policy entanglement between tenant-level burst credits and route-based quota assignment caused temporary reclassification of Aventra requests into a lower-burst window. That lowered the available prefix credits and triggered request shaping at ~200 rps, producing the 429 flood and increased latency due to queueing.

Technical summary (short):
- Root cause: a recent policy refresh merged two routing rule sets (hosted-default and env-dedicated) without the proper precedence. The combined rule set assigned Aventra to a route expecting hosted-burst semantics but evaluated against dedicated-pool credit accounting.
- Symptom mapping: rapid token-per-second debt, request shaping at the gateway, and KV cache thrash under backpressure (explains the p95 jump).

Immediate remediation executed (09:58 PDT):
1) Rolled back the routing precedence change to the prior evaluation order (hotfix commit c9b1e2).
2) Temporarily increased Aventra's per-tenant burst window to 30s and bumped the prefix credit cap by 2x.
3) Enabled short-term route whitelist to prevent automated policy refreshes against that tenant for 4 hours.

Observed impact: 10 minutes after the rollback we saw p95 drop from 1.8s to ~420ms and 429 rate drop below 0.5%. There are a handful of lingering rejections for long-running batched jobs — we're tracing those.

Next steps (owner/time):
- (Neha) Run a full policy precedence test and validation suite across dedicated/hosted pools by EOD (INF-2137).
- (Connor) Add a gated canary for policy refreshes targeting any tenant with >50k rps and enforce a traffic shadow validation.
- (Marissa) Exec update and recommendation for one-off credit / SLA mitigation for Aventra.

Samir — apologies for the disruption. We are keeping this a P1 and will provide a short postmortem with config diffs and suggested guardrails by EOD.

Neha Kapoor
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.io
From: marissa_cole@redwood.io
To: product_ops@redwood.io, finance_ops@redwood.io
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.io, neha_kapoor@redwood.io, connor_obrien@redwood.io
Date: Tue, 7 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive note — Aventra Labs incident and proposed customer remediation

Quick executive summary: Aventra Labs experienced production latency spikes and elevated 429s due to a policy precedence regression in a routing refresh. Neha's team has rolled back the change and applied a short-term override; customer impact reduced substantially within ~10 minutes.

Business impact / ask:
- Aventra is an active enterprise prospect in contract stage (DEAL-4982). Risk: reduced confidence; ask from customer for credit and a written SLA mitigation.
- Proposal: approve a one-off goodwill credit equal to 1 week of average usage and a formal joint remediation plan (postmortem + validation run). Estimated credit cost: ~$12k.

Please confirm approval for the credit and for a co-branded postmortem to be delivered to Aventra by EOD tomorrow. I recommend we also pause automated policy refreshes for any tenants in 'high-risk' deals until we have the gated canary in place.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Two asks from Aventra:
1) We'd like a short incident call tomorrow to review the policy precedence test plan and the gating/canary approach.
2) Please confirm the proposed credit and provide a draft postmortem and timeline for permanent guardrails.

Appreciate the responsiveness — this helped avoid a demo failure.
